claims.head: Who blinks first?
claims.body: The Oilers are the league’s best for the power play, but the Hurricanes are one of the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Oilers’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots. Edmonton has had one of the league’s most effective power plays, and Carolina has had one of the league’s best penalty kills for years.

claims.head: The Hurricanes roll four lines, the Oilers lean on their top six
claims.body: On depth, Carolina is one of the league’s best, but Edmonton is the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. If this one comes down to the bottom six, that suits the Hurricanes.

notes.text: Logan Stankoven has started killing penalties: on the ice for 35% of the team’s shorthanded time in 11 games, up from 1% last season.

faceoff.text: Jordan Staal is sent out to take power-play faceoffs, then changes. He has taken 27% of the team’s power-play draws but stays on for about 20 seconds at a time, against 69 for the regulars, and is most often replaced by Nikolaj Ehlers (13 of 16 changes).

notes.text: Kasperi Kapanen has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 53% of the team’s power-play time in 9 games, up from 6% last season.
Ty Emberson is no longer killing penalties: 2% of the team’s shorthanded time in 7 games, down from 30% last season.

stakes: The Hurricanes go in first in the NHL with 17 points, the Oilers second in the Pacific with 15 points.

EDM.head: A slightly uphill night for the Oilers
EDM.body: Even though Edmonton has home-ice advantage, Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Oilers can tip it if they get good looks.

CAR.head: Leaning the Hurricanes’ way
CAR.body: Even though Edmonton has home-ice advantage, Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Oilers can still swing it if they get good looks.

story.head: A good test for both
paras: The Oilers have won two in a row. The Hurricanes are 8-2-1. Two good teams meet.

It’s strength against strength: the Oilers are the league’s best for the power play, but the Hurricanes are one of the best at the penalty kill. The Hurricanes roll four lines, but the Oil lean on their top six.

items.text: Nikolaj Ehlers is one point from 600.
Zach Hyman has seven goals in six games against Carolina since 2023-24.
The Oilers have been without Frederik Andersen for several games, and have had to make do without Matt Savoie all season. Devon Levi is expected to start.
The Hurricanes are newly without Mark Jankowski, and have been without Taylor Hall since Oct 13.
